title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - UCC: Rights of Buyer
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A vendor delivers a shipment of goods to a public agency, but the buyer notices the items do not meet the exact specifications of the contract. The buyer rejects the delivery. Under the UCC, what right does the vendor generally have if the contract performance time has not yet expired?
options: The right to cancel the contract without penalty
The right to sue for specific performance
The right to cure the defect
The right to force the buyer to accept a discount
questions.explain: Under the UCC, if a buyer rejects a nonconforming delivery and the contract time for performance has not yet expired, the seller has a 'right to cure'—meaning they can notify the buyer of their intent to provide conforming goods within the original contract timeframe.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which of the following describes the UCC principle that allows a buyer to reject goods entirely if they fail in any respect to conform to the contract?
questions.explain: The 'Perfect Tender Rule' under the UCC allows buyers of goods to reject the delivery if the goods or the tender of delivery fail in any respect to conform to the contract.
